name: Event Hubs
tagline: An Azure Event Hubs namespace the official SDKs talk to over AMQP: partitions, consumer groups, owner levels, checkpoints and throttling on cue, with a Kafka endpoint too.
stands_in_for: Pub/Sub import topics from Event Hubs

capabilities.title: Partitions like the service
capabilities.text: A partition key goes where the service sends it (lookup3 hash); no key, round-robin; a batch lands in one partition.

capabilities.title: Read from anywhere
capabilities.text: Receivers start at the beginning, @latest, after an offset or sequence number, or at an enqueued time.

capabilities.title: Consumer groups
capabilities.text: $Default plus the groups you create; at most 5 receivers per partition and group, as in Azure.

capabilities.title: Owner levels
capabilities.text: A receiver with a higher epoch takes the partition; the older one is disconnected with link stolen.

capabilities.title: Checkpoints you can see
capabilities.text: BlobCheckpointStore blobs in a Stuntman Storage account show next to each partition's reader.

capabilities.title: Management answers
capabilities.text: get_eventhub_properties and get_partition_properties: begin and last sequence number, last offset, empty.

capabilities.title: Retention on the clock
capabilities.text: Events older than the hub's retention go when you move the environment clock; begin sequence moves on.

capabilities.title: Kafka endpoint
capabilities.text: Kafka clients log in with $ConnectionString and read and write the same partitions as AMQP clients.

capabilities.title: Feeds Pub/Sub
capabilities.text: A Pub/Sub import topic naming the hub reads it: partition key as ordering key, properties as attributes.

excerpts.title: A hub: its partitions and every event with who sent it

callouts.title: Hubs
callouts.text: The namespace's event hubs with partitions, consumer groups and events kept.

callouts.title: Two doors
callouts.text: AMQP on the Service Bus port, and Kafka through Streams' port.

callouts.title: Partitions
callouts.text: Begin and last sequence number of each partition; click one to see only its events.

callouts.title: Partition key
callouts.text: Sequence number, byte offset and the key that picked the partition.

callouts.title: Who sent it
callouts.text: The app over AMQP or Kafka apart from you and the agent.

excerpts.title: Send, provoke, and the readers of each partition

callouts.title: Send events
callouts.text: Body, properties, a partition key or a partition, as another producer would.

callouts.title: Server busy
callouts.text: The next sends answer com.microsoft:server-busy; the SDKs send again.

callouts.title: Steal owner
callouts.text: Readers lose their partition as if a higher epoch came.

callouts.title: Owner level
callouts.text: Each receiver reading now, its epoch and the last sequence number sent.

callouts.title: Checkpoint behind
callouts.text: The app's BlobCheckpointStore checkpoint, amber when it trails the reader.

provoke.name: Server busy
provoke.what: The next N sends and management requests answer com.microsoft:server-busy

provoke.name: Quota exceeded
provoke.what: The next N sends are rejected with QuotaExceeded

provoke.name: Slow sends
provoke.what: Each send waits before it is accepted

provoke.name: Entity not found
provoke.what: A hub answers not found to links and management

provoke.name: Partition owner stolen
provoke.what: Readers of a hub are disconnected with amqp:link:stolen

provoke.name: Higher epoch
provoke.what: A second receiver with a higher owner level takes the partition

provoke.name: Connection drop
provoke.what: Every connection of the namespace closes; the SDKs reconnect

provoke.name: Wrong key
provoke.what: With any_key off, tokens not signed by a policy key get 401

provoke.name: Events expire
provoke.what: Events older than the hub's retention go

advantages.title: No Azure subscription
advantages.text: No namespace to provision or pay for; hubs exist the moment create_eventhub runs.

advantages.title: Throttling when you want
advantages.text: ServerBusy and QuotaExceeded on the next send, not when a real namespace happens to hit its limit.

advantages.title: Epochs you can watch
advantages.text: See which receiver owns each partition and its checkpoint, instead of guessing from logs.

advantages.title: Days pass in seconds
advantages.text: Retention runs on the environment clock: test what expired events do without waiting a day.

agent.prompt: Check that our order consumer survives a throttled Event Hubs and resumes from its checkpoint.
steps: partition 0 · sequence 412 · sent by the app after 2 retries
